name: Simvoly
tagline: Websites, funnels, ecommerce, memberships, and CRM in one platform

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1 website, 0 funnels, 1 domain, unlimited pages, 20 GB bandwidth, 100 community members, 100 subscribers/1,200 emails, 5 hosted videos
tiers.notes: E-commerce is not included by default; it is offered as an add-on.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 1 website, 5 funnels, 6 domains, 60 GB bandwidth, 100 products, 100 members, 100 subscribers/1,200 emails, 5 videos

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: 1 website, 10 funnels, 11 domains, 100 GB bandwidth, unlimited products, 1,000 community members, 1,000 subscribers/12,000 emails, 20 videos

tiers.name: Elite
tiers.limits: 5 websites, unlimited funnels/domains, 200 GB bandwidth, unlimited products, 5,000 community members, 2,500 subscribers/30,000 emails, 50 videos

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual equivalents shown by vendor)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Websites, funnels, bandwidth, communities, ecommerce, videos, admins and marketing subscribers can require add-ons. Subscriber add-ons run from $9/month for +500 to $1,499/month for +500,000; email overage is $0.80 per 1,000.

verdictSummary: The visible website + funnel builder loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Simvoly earns its keep through editor, CMS, hosting, polish, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused website + funnel builder generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Simvoly: A single site is easy to code. People pay for safe ongoing edits, templates, publishing, domains, collaboration, and no-maintenance hosting.
ongoingBurden: Maintain responsive rendering, browser compatibility, deployment, domains, forms, spam protection, backups, and editor migrations.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Websites, funnels, products, memberships, email and CRM on a real free plan; one custom domain and one course.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A page-editor framework, not an all-in-one site, funnel, store and CRM.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Odoo Community
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Website, store and CRM are present; creator funnels and simple membership delivery are not a clean free workflow.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Vvveb
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The site, store and subscriptions fit; funnels and CRM do not.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Simvoly is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Simvoly, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a focused website + funnel builder generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: managed hosting, forms, and analytics; general-purpose visual editing; large template and component libraries.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
